npc.xenolinguist.flavor_text: The station says the signal isn't human. If there's a reference dataset out there, it could crack the whole thing open. Bring it to me.
step.lab_q1_sample.completion_flavor: The fragment is secured. Its surface carries a repeating pattern that looks less like a manufacture mark than a remembered response. Deliver it to the Research Officer on Mercury before the pattern changes again.
step.lab_q1_sample.description: The reasearch team needs more data. Return to the alien console on Mars and attach the data extractor. Once it completes its diagnostics, return the device back to the labs.
step.lab_q1_sample.title: The Sample
step.lab_q2_delivery.completion_flavor: Data extraction was extremely successful. The researches have terrabytes of data to process. This may take some time.
step.lab_q2_delivery.description: The data is extracted and in your hold. Deliver it to the researchers on Mercury.
step.lab_q2_delivery.dialogue.research_o: The data is in your mission hold. Hand it over and let the researchers begin deciphering it.
You took the fragment without disturbing the seal. Good. Hand it over. If its signature matches the transmission, we may be able to ask the door to open without pretending we understand it.
step.lab_q2_delivery.ready_message: The lab has a working hypothesis: the console may correspond to an alien device preserved at Procyon C.
step.lab_q2_delivery.title: The Delivery
step.lab_q3_reference.completion_flavor: The cache contains various bits and trinkets, including a tool with the same undulation as the tech near the Mars site. Deliver the tool to the xenolinguist at Alpha Centauri's Science Port. She may be able to determine how the two are connected.
step.lab_q3_reference.description: Travel to Procyon C. A sealed cache beneath the outpost holds an alien device. Filed away with no known use, recover it from the ice caves so the lab can test it against this new data.
step.lab_q3_reference.dialogue.research_: The material is answering at a frequency no human instrument should survive recording. We need the Procyon C reference cache to learn whether that frequency belongs to the door, the signal, or something farther along the route. Recover the dataset intact.
step.lab_q3_reference.title: The Connection
step.lab_q4_xenolinguist.completion_flav: The xenolinguist finds a match, but not a translation. The two patterns share a route through the same dead frequencies. One more dataset may complete the map: a derelict near Sirius carried a reference recorder. The Research Officer will call when the coordinates are triangulated.
step.lab_q4_xenolinguist.description: The ancient alien tool is in your mission hold. Take it to the xenolinguist at Alpha Centauri's Science Port. She will examine the tool against the extracted data and determine the connection between them.
step.lab_q4_xenolinguist.dialogue.resear: If that dataset copy goes missing, the lab keeps a backup of the Procyon reference files - I can issue another. Get it straight to the Science Port.
Request another copy of the dataset
step.lab_q4_xenolinguist.dialogue.xenoli: The cross-reference gives us a route, not a meaning. One more dataset may show where the route terminates. The Research Officer is triangulating a derelict near Sirius.

You brought the reference dataset. It does not translate the signal; it shows us where the signal stops behaving like a message. Hand it over. I can map the shared frequency, but I will not call that map a key until we know what it opens.
step.lab_q4_xenolinguist.ready_message: The coordinates are triangulated: a scout vessel lost near Sirius, its reference recorder still broadcasting a narrow pulse. Recover the recorder and bring it to the Research Officer on Mercury. The wreck has been quiet for decades; quiet does not mean unguarded.
step.lab_q4_xenolinguist.title: The Xenolinguist
step.lab_q5_frequency.completion_flavor: The recorder is intact. Its last transmission contains a frequency that answers the Mars sample, then points away from human space. Bring it to the Research Officer on Mercury before anyone edits the record.
step.lab_q5_frequency.description: A derelict scout vessel near Sirius carries the final reference recorder. Recover it from the wreck and bring back the evidence intact. The pirates guarding it may think they are protecting salvage; they may be protecting the last quiet warning in human space.
step.lab_q5_frequency.dialogue.research_: The derelict is near Sirius, a scout vessel lost decades ago. A pirate captain and his raiders are stripping it now. Clear them, board the wreck, and recover the frequency recorder before its final signal disappears.

The xenolinguist's route map is nearly complete. A derelict scout vessel near Sirius carried a reference-frequency recorder, and a pirate captain with raiders is already picking it over. Recover the recorder before the last quiet evidence is scattered across the system.
step.lab_q5_frequency.title: The Frequency
step.lab_q6_return.completion_flavor: The recorder is handed over intact. The route is complete; the meaning is not. The lab will forge a resonance key and contact you when it is ready.
step.lab_q6_return.description: The reference recorder is in your mission hold. Return to Mercury and deliver it to the Research Officer. It completes the route map leading away from Mars.
step.lab_q6_return.dialogue.research_off: The recorder is in your mission hold. Hand it over and the route map is complete. The key can be forged, though the lab still does not know what it will wake.
The recorder survived. It completes the route map, not the meaning behind it. Hand it over and we will build the resonance key without pretending that a key tells us why a door exists.
step.lab_q6_return.ready_message: The resonance key is forged. It matches the door's material so precisely that the instruments register a reply before anyone activates it. Report to the Research Officer on Mercury. The key is waiting.
step.lab_q6_return.title: The Return
step.lab_q7_key.description: Return to the Research Officer on Mercury. The resonance key is forged from the door's material signature. Take it to Mars and ask the door what it has been waiting for.
step.lab_q7_key.dialogue.research_office: There it is - the resonance key. Forged from the door's own material signature and calibrated against data older than human contact with this region. Take it to Mars. The door should open. What comes after may be a discovery, a warning, or a question that has been waiting longer than we have.
step.lab_q7_key.title: The Key
